# Background

This script is created for **Caroline Stockwell** by Ayrianna Hedgecock at UNC FCCF. The script will take raw spectral FCS files and unmix them.

### To-Dos

- enviornment init/ package checklist to transfer to new computer

```{r}
#| label: packages used
library(tidyverse)
library(AutoSpectral)
library(AutoSpectralRcpp)
library(Luciernaga)
library(openCyto)
library(flowWorkspace)
library(flowGate)
```

- Update the `file.path()` if needed
  - Let's switch to something more flexible by using a .yml file to configure folder names
- Place all the single color controls in the folder labelled "SCC"
- Place all samples in the folder labelled "Samples"



```{r}
#| label: file paths

analysis_config_location <- file.path("AnalysisInfo")
parameters_file <- list.files(
  analysis_config_location,
  "\\.yml$",
  full.names = TRUE
)
analysis_parameters <- yaml::read_yaml(parameters_file)

input_folder <- file.path(analysis_parameters$input_folder)
output_folder <- file.path(analysis_parameters$output_folder)
single_color_control_folder <- file.path(
  input_folder,
  analysis_parameters$single_color_controls_folder
)
samples_folder <- file.path(input_folder, analysis_parameters$samples_folder)
unmixed_folder <- file.path(output_folder, analysis_parameters$unmixed_folder)
```


```{r}
#| label: More set up

Patient_unstained_samples <- list.files(
    single_color_control_folder,
    pattern = analysis_parameters$patient_sample_pattern,
    full.names = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
)

Patient_samples <- list.files(
    path = samples_folder,
    pattern = analysis_parameters$patient_sample_pattern,
    full.names = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
)

CleanUpGatingTemplateFile <- list.files(
    path = analysis_config_location,
    pattern = analysis_parameters$gatingTemplate,
    full.names = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
)
```

# AutoSpectral

Set the spectral cytometer settings

```{r}
#| label: Spectral Cytometer settings

asp <- get.autospectral.param(cytometer = "aurora")
control.dir <- single_color_control_folder
control_filename <- list.files(
  path = output_folder,
  pattern = analysis_parameters$AutoSpectral_control_file_name,
  full.names = TRUE,

```

### Create a control file

MOVE THIS SECTION TO README OR A SETUP FILE. should also explain folder structure. 
There is a ShinyApp to help with the control process. ONLY one (1) "AF" sample can be identified. This should be that patient the matrix will be used for.

**I should move this to the README as setup** Then the control filename will already be entered. 

```{r}
#| label: Shiny Helper App AutoSpectral. Creates and validates the control file. 
#| eval: false
shiny::runApp(appDir = input_folder, launch.browser = TRUE)
```

This file was saved to the Data Folder initally, then manually moved to the Outputs folder (during testing)

To do this the Manual/programatic Way:

```{r}
#| label: Create Control file manually
#| eval: false

create.control.file(
  control.dir,
  asp,
  output.dir = output_folder,
  filename = analysis_parameters$AutoSpectral_control_file_name
)
```

If fluorophores exist in the `AutoSpectral` database they will be autofilled in the contol .csv. If not, you will need to manually add it in.

Structure of the Control File

See Control File information here: [Control File- AutoSpectral](https://drcytometer.github.io/AutoSpectral/articles/02_Control_File_example.html) The main structural elements to the control file are the following columns. Note, we will be using the `get.spectra.automated()` function, so the "legacy" columns are not needed. Read more in linked article.

- **filename**: The actual .fcs filename
- **fluorophore**: The name of the fluorophore (or AF in case of the unstained)
- **marker**: The name of the marker (or left empty in the case of the unstained)
- **channel**: The peak detector channel of the fluorophore (left empty for the unstained).
- **control.type**: Whether the unmixing control is cells or beads (used for matching positive and negatives for background subtraction)
- **universal.negative**: By default empty, if you want to use an universal negative, copy the filename of the corresponding unstained into this spot on a per fluorophore basis
- large.gate: Logical value, by default FALSE, set to TRUE to expand the gating area
- gate.name: Gate name for use in signature retrievel
- gate.define: Logical, permits you to set the general gate region as defined by gate.name
- is.viability: Whether your control is a viability dye.

Edit the file as necessary. I find this easiest within the .csv rather than programtically in R. In the future, we can add programtic edits.

Now that the control file has been edited, lets maunally save it with the \*\*"\_updated"\*\* suffix so it doesn't get overwritten in future runs of this script.

### Validate control file

This only needs to be done if the Shiny App was **NOT** used. QC the control file:

```{r}
#| label: Manual control file needs to be validated if before moving forward

issues <- check.control.file(
  control.dir,
  control.def.file = control_filename,
  asp
)
```

### Spectral Extraction

Let's clean and extract our signatures

```{r}
#| label: Extract spectra
#| eval: false

full_control.dir <- normalizePath(control.dir, mustWork = TRUE)
full_control_filename <- normalizePath(control_filename, mustWork = TRUE)

spectra <- withr::with_dir(
  output_folder,
  get.spectra.automated(
    control.dir = full_control.dir,
    control.def.file = full_control_filename,
    asp = asp,
    figures = TRUE,
    verbose = FALSE
  )
)
```

Figures are automatically created to QC this process. The folders created from this step 
This should be a stopping point to ensure all looks good!

## Unmixing

Let's create a "flow.control" object to feed dye names and markers into unmixing

```{r}
#| label: create flow.control and reload spectra if needed
#| eval: false
flow_control <- reload.flow.control(control.dir, control_filename, asp)

if (!exists("spectra", envir = .GlobalEnv)) {
    table_spectra_folder <- file.path(output_folder, "table_spectra")

    spectra_files <- list.files(table_spectra_folder, full.names = FALSE)
    automated_spectra_file <- spectra_files[1] # make sure this is the correct file, it should be.

    spectra <- read.spectra(
        spectra.file = automated_spectra_file,
        spectra.dir = table_spectra_folder
    )
}
```

Hmm, should it actually be, if the spectra doesn't exist in the files, then run the above code. IF it does then call it in... so something like:

```{r}
#| label: combine above code blocks

table_spectra_folder <- file.path(output_folder, "table_spectra")
existing_spectra_files <- list.files(
  table_spectra_folder,
  pattern = "^Automated_autospectral_spectra_[0-9]{8}_[0-9]{6}\\.csv$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

if (base::length(existing_spectra_files) > 0) {
  file_info <- file.info(existing_spectra_files)
  # If several files exist, use the most recently modified one

  latest_file <- rownames(
    file_info[which.max(file_info$mtime), , drop = FALSE]
  )

  spectra <- read.spectra(
    spectra.file = basename(latest_file),
    spectra.dir = dirname(latest_file)
  )
  message("Using spectra file: ", basename(latest_file))
} else {
  # if no file exists, create
  full_control.dir <- normalizePath(control.dir, mustWork = TRUE)
  full_control_filename <- normalizePath(control_filename, mustWork = TRUE)

  spectra <- withr::with_dir(
    output_folder,
    get.spectra.automated(
      control.dir = full_control.dir,
      control.def.file = full_control_filename,
      asp = asp,
      figures = TRUE,
      verbose = FALSE
    )
  )
}

flow_control <- reload.flow.control(control.dir, control_filename, asp)

```

The above code looks really good - Let's chuck the flow.conrol here and this is the code we will use

This is a complicated sample, let's leverage the per-cell and per-fluorophore extraction to get best unmixing we can.

Let's start with the AF extractions per pt


```{r}
#| label: Extract AF from patient samples
#| eval: false

plot.dir <- file.path(output_folder, "figure_autofluorscence")

patient_af <- map(
  Patient_unstained_samples,
  \(sample) {
    get.af.spectra(
      unstained.sample = sample,
      asp = asp,
      spectra = spectra,
      plot.dir = plot.dir,
      table.dir = table_spectra_folder,
      verbose = FALSE
    )
  }
)
```

Test went well, let's move to per-cell fluorophore optimization

like above, let's combine the 3 blocks

```{r}
#| label: fluorophore optimization

existing_variant_RDS <- list.files(
  path = output_folder,
  pattern = "\\.rds$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

if (base::length(existing_variant_RDS) > 0) {

  fluorophore_variants <- get.spectral.variants(

    asp = asp,
    spectra = spectra,
    output.dir = output_folder

}
```

### ADD PRESENTATION/REPORT TO VIEW FLUOROPHORE VARIANTS


Now, let's put both pieces together to do the final unmix


```{r}
#| label: run full unmixing
#| eval: false

Patient_sample <- list.files(samples_folder, full.names = TRUE)

unmix.fcs(
  fcs.file = Patient_sample[1], #one example
  spectra = spectra,
  asp = asp,
  flow.control = flow_control,
  method = "AutoSpectral",
  af.spectra = patient_af,
  spectra.variants = fluorophore_variants,
  speed = "slow",
  output.dir = unmixed_folder
)
```


```{r}
#| label: Apply unmixing to all the patients

# link patient af files with PT names
patient_ids_af <- str_extract(
  basename(Patient_unstained_samples),
  "PT[0-9]+"
)

if (anyNA(patient_ids_af)) {
  stop("At least one unstained sample is missing a patient ID.")
}

names(patient_af) <- patient_ids_af

# AF file names
af_files <- list.files(
  path = table_spectra_folder,
  pattern = "Autofluorescence spectra.*\\.csv$",
  full.names = FALSE,
  ignore.case = TRUE
)

if (length(af_files) == 0) {
  stop("No autofluorescence CSV files found in: ", table_spectra_folder)
}

af_patient_ids <- str_extract(
  basename(af_files),
  "PT[0-9]+"
)

if (anyNA(af_patient_ids)) {
  stop("At least one AF filename is missing a patient ID.")
}

# Check for duplicate AF files
if (anyDuplicated(af_patient_ids) > 0) {
  duplicate_ids <- unique(
    af_patient_ids[duplicated(af_patient_ids)]
  )

  stop(
    "Multiple AF files found for: ",
    paste(duplicate_ids, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

names(af_files) <- af_patient_ids

# Check that every PT has a corresponding AF file
missing_af_files <- setdiff(names(patient_af), names(af_files))
if (length(missing_af_files) > 0) {
  stop(
    "No AF file found for: ",
    paste(missing_af_files, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# Reorder AF files to match patient_af
af_files <- af_files[names(patient_af)]

# unmix
Patient_samples # files to be unmixed


unmixTest <- function(sample) {
  patient_id_sample <- str_extract(
    basename(sample),
    "PT[0-9]+"
  )

  if (is.na(patient_id_sample)) {
    stop(
      "Could not identify patient ID in sample: ",
      basename(sample)
    )
  }

  if (!patient_id_sample %in% names(patient_af)) {
    stop("No AF spectra found for patient: ", patient_id_sample)
  }

  af_for_patient <- patient_af[[patient_id_sample]]
  af_file_used <- af_files[[patient_id_sample]]

  message("Unmixing sample: ", basename(sample))
  message("Using AF file: ", basename(af_file_used))

  cli::cli_alert_success(
    paste("Unmixing sample:", basename(sample))
  )

  cli::cli_alert_success(
    paste("Using AF file:", basename(af_file_used))
  )

  AutoSpectral::unmix.fcs(
    fcs.file = sample,
    spectra = spectra,
    asp = asp,
    flow.control = flow_control,
    method = "AutoSpectral",
    af.spectra = af_for_patient,
    spectra.variants = fluorophore_variants,
    speed = "slow",
    output.dir = unmixed_folder,
    verbose = FALSE,
    pipeline = "joint",
    estimate.time = FALSE
  )
}

unmixTest(Patient_samples[1])

walk(Patient_samples, unmixTest)
```


Now that we've completed the unmixing of one file, let's check our work!

Let's do some basic clean up gates prior to visualizing the NxN plot

See how to write the gating Template [here](https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/3.24/bioc/vignettes/openCyto/inst/doc/HowToWriteCSVTemplate.html)

```{r}
#| label: Load OpenCyto Gating Template

GatingFolder <- file.path("openCytoGate")
CleanUpGatingTemplateFile <- list.files(
  GatingFolder,
  pattern = ".csv",
  full.names = TRUE
)
cleanup_gates <- data.table::fread(CleanUpGatingTemplateFile)
Template <- gatingTemplate(cleanup_gates)
```

# QC unmixing

## automated gating set up

Let's do some basic clean up gates prior to visualizing the NxN plot

See how to write the gating Template [here](https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/3.24/bioc/vignettes/openCyto/inst/doc/HowToWriteCSVTemplate.html)

```{r}
#| label: Load OpenCyto Gating Template

cleanup_gates <- data.table::fread(CleanUpGatingTemplateFile)
Template <- gatingTemplate(cleanup_gates)
```

### GatingSet and Transformation

```{r}
#| label: Create GatingSet & transform

# locate unmixed files
unmixed_files <- list.files(unmixed_folder, full.names = TRUE)

# load in as a cytoset
patient_cytoset <- load_cytoset_from_fcs(
  unmixed_files,
  truncate_max_range = FALSE,
  transformation = FALSE
)

# create GatingSet for gates
patient_GS <- GatingSet(patient_cytoset)
```

```{r}
#| label: transform data

# list of fluorophores in files
parameters <- colnames(patient_GS)
flurophores_only <- parameters[!str_detect(parameters, "Time|FSC|SSC|Index")]
flurophores_only

# transformation
Biexponential <- flowjo_biexp_trans(
  channelRange = 4096,
  maxValue = 262144,
  pos = 4.5,
  neg = 0,
  widthBasis = -1000
)
BiexTransformList <- transformerList(flurophores_only, Biexponential)

transform(patient_GS, BiexTransformList)
```

```{r}
#| label: View transformation

Luciernaga::Utility_NbyNPlots(
    patient_GS,
    sample.name = "TUBENAME",
    outpath = output_folder,
    ycolumn = "SSC-A",
    bins = 300,
    returntype = "patchwork"
)

ggcyto(patient_GS[1], subset = "root", aes(x = "FSC-A", y = "SSC-A")) +
    geom_hex(bins = 1000)

ggcyto(patient_GS[1], subset = "singletsSSC", aes(x = "FSC-A")) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 1000)
```

### Apply automated gating scheme

```{r}
#| label: Run automated gating

gt_gating(Template, patient_GS)
```

```{r}
#| label: Check gating
```

### Adjust gates as needed

Let's try a manual cleanup gate

The "singletsFSC" is too narrow for me - let's adjust

```{r}

```

```{r}

#| eval: false
gs_gate_interactive_adjust(
  gs = patient_GS,
  gate = "singletsFSC",
  sample = 1,
  AdjustAll = TRUE
)

Utility_GatingPlots(
  patient_GS,
  sample.name = "GUID",
  gtFile = cleanup_gates,
  returnType = "patchwork",
  removestrings = ".fcs"
)
```

```{r}

#| eval: false

save_gs(patient_GS, path = gs_save_path)

load_gs(gs_save_path)
```

## CompensAID package

Is the comepsAID package useful?

```{r}
#| label: get flowframe

gated_data_flowframe <- gh_pop_get_data(
  patient_GS[[1]],
  y = "singletsSSC",
  inverse.transform = FALSE
)

ff <- cytoframe_to_flowFrame(gated_data_flowframe)

ff[, names(markernames(ff))]
```

```{r}
library(CompensAID)
```

```{r}
#| label: Run Compensaid and visualize
compensaid_results <- CompensAID(ff)
compensaid_matirx <- PlotMatrix(compensaid_results)
compensaid_matirx
```

```{r}
#| label: View flagged pairs

# Check SSI < -1
index <- which(compensaid_results$matrix < -1, arr.ind = TRUE)

combination <- data.frame(
  primary.channel = rownames(compensaid_results$matrix)[index[, "col"]],
  secondary.channel = rownames(compensaid_results$matrix)[index[, "row"]]
) |>
  mutate(
    primary.marker = markernames(ff)[primary.channel],
    secondary.marker = markernames(ff)[secondary.channel]
  )

compensaid_plots <- pmap(
  combination[c("primary.marker", "secondary.marker")],
  \(primary.marker, secondary.marker) {
    PlotDotSSI(
      compensaid_results,
      ff,
      primary = primary.marker,
      secondary = secondary.marker,
      showScores = TRUE
    )
  }
)

walk(compensaid_plots, print)
```

This is potentially very powerful!
